solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Managed to get inside revolutionary egg farm

indicators.note: the word for managed is placed within the turned-round egg
something revolutionary turns over, so the word egg is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned
managed, as in ran a business, gives RAN

explanation.surface: Someone who has organised a revolution in egg production takes over a poultry farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives GGE; 'farm' at the end is the definition, not part of the egg farming picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings, so it stands as a synonym for a farm.

clue.text: Return game in Japan needs support

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game played with black and white stones
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A player wants backing before travelling home for a Japanese board game.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back means to return to a place, a phrasal synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Plant, iris, a team transmuted

indicators.note: transmuted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An alchemist turns an iris and a whole team into some other plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transmuted' rearranges IRIS A TEAM, nine letters, into the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic plants including wormwood and mugwort, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: One using putty, good at first then less inclined to work?

parts.note: lazier describes someone with even less appetite for work

explanation.surface: A workman who starts off well but becomes idler, perhaps from handling putty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' places G at the front, and 'then' brings in the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass in window frames is bedded with putty, so a tradesman fitting panes is one who uses it.

clue.text: Clearly identified remedy

definitions.meaning: precise and explicitly stated, as an adjective
an old term for a medicine that treats one particular disease

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both precisely stated and, as a noun, a medicine aimed at a given ailment.

clue.text: Feel sorry for yours, at the start, positioned behind mine

indicators.note: the first letter of yours comes after the word for a mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word yours is used

explanation.surface: A miner commiserates with a friend whose shaft lies behind his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' takes Y from yours; 'positioned behind' puts it after PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity someone is to feel compassion or sorrow at their misfortune, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Arrests party in police station

parts.note: to cop someone is slang for arresting them, so arrests gives COPS
a hop is an informal dance or party

explanation.surface: Revellers at a party are arrested and taken to the station.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop shop is informal slang for a police station.

clue.text: Sort of group in centre

definitions.meaning: a type of group assembled to discuss a product, a market-research panel
the central point of interest or attention

explanation.definitionFit: A focus group is a market-research panel, and a focus is also the central point of attention.

clue.text: Pace might get star bowled out

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for bowled is removed

parts.note: a celebrity is a star of screen or sport
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A famous player's speed may see him dismissed in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes B (bowled, in cricket scoring) from CELEBRITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness of movement, a formal synonym for speed or pace.

clue.text: Risk money on fish shop

parts.note: to bet is to stake money on an outcome
a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: Someone gambles cash on a fishmonger's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a noun for a store but is the slang verb, to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, to shop someone is to inform on them to the police, which is to betray them.

clue.text: Unconventional play — Act I most odd

indicators.note: the phrase most odd signals the letters are put into a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds the opening act of an avant-garde play very strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most odd' rearranges PLAY ACT I into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, a direct synonym for unconventional or unusual.

clue.text: Clip more off setter

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are out of order or gone wrong

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim even more from someone who sets things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CLIP MORE into the word for a crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter is also called its compiler, the person who puts the puzzle together.

clue.text: Complete collection of religious books found in Ireland

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the scriptures is placed within the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full set of scriptures turns up in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete collection' reads as one phrase, but 'Complete' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Charles and the Queen making a drink

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A royal couple prepares a drink together.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken after another, such as beer after a shot of spirits.

clue.text: Got the shakes in skid row?

indicators.note: shakes suggests the letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A down-and-out has developed a tremor while living rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakes' rearranges GOT THE. The question mark marks skid row, a run-down district, as an example only.
explanation.definitionFit: Skid row is a run-down urban area of the destitute, a kind of slum quarter.

clue.text: Allow something not usually acceptable, a tip on time in prison

indicators.note: on places the pieces after the prison term in the across entry

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
the point is the sharp tip of something

explanation.surface: An inmate is advised to put a sharp end on his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: A stretch is British slang for a prison sentence; 'on' means the tip follows it in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to bend the rules and permit something beyond normal limits.

clue.text: Bury game — training cut short

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
RU is rugby union
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A football club, Bury, sees its training session brought to an early end.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also an English football town, which makes 'game' look like football.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt is to break in on and so cut short a speaker or activity.

clue.text: European health resort empty after uprising

parts.note: a spa is a resort with healing waters

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising turns the word upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: A spa town is deserted after a popular revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' gives NIARD, read upward in a down entry; 'European' is defined broadly, a Spaniard being one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is a person from Spain, so an example of a European.

clue.text: Pretend to be uninterested in baffling drama?

definitions.meaning: to feign indifference, especially to someone's advances
a play that is difficult to understand, a theatre piece tough to grasp

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means feigning lack of interest, and taken literally describes a play that is tough to understand.

clue.text: That woman's name raised as one holding unorthodox opinions

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means turned upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A woman's name is brought up as a dissenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives ETIC, read upward in a down entry; 'as' merely links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds beliefs contrary to established religious doctrine.

clue.text: An angel, girl entertaining barrister fellow rejected

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the girl surrounds the rest

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: rejected signals the abbreviation for fellow is thrown out

parts.note: a brief is slang for a barrister

explanation.surface: A woman hosts a lawyer whose companion has been turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' leaves BRIE; calling a barrister a brief is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel of the Bible who announced the birth of Jesus.

clue.text: Evergreen tree with crack in it, blown over

indicators.note: blown over turns the whole tree upward in this down entry, reading backwards
in places the attempt inside the tree

parts.note: the elm is a deciduous tree
to have a crack at something is to try it

explanation.surface: A tree with a split in its trunk is felled in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives ELTRYM, and 'blown over' fells that tree, reading it backwards; 'Evergreen' alone is the definition, not 'Evergreen tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers, used here as an example.

clue.text: Kind disposition

definitions.meaning: a sort or type, as a noun
a person's inborn temperament or character

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sort or type and also a person's innate character.

clue.text: Cast in the short series

indicators.note: short means the word the loses its last letter

parts.note: a row is a series of things in a line

explanation.surface: Actors appear in a brief run of shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' gives TH; 'Cast' looks like actors but is the verb to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast and to throw both mean to fling something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Foolish constable found in frightful bog in part of Ulster

indicators.note: the scrambled bog sits inside the Ulster place name

parts.note: Derry is a city and county in Northern Ireland, part of Ulster

indicators.note: frightful suggests the letters of bog are badly messed up

explanation.surface: A dim policeman turns up in a dreadful Irish bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' gives OGB; Derry, also called Londonderry, is a city and county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.

clue.text: Prejudice shown by one in HQ out east

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the shortened headquarters
out removes the letter for east

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
E is the compass abbreviation for east
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Discrimination shown by someone at headquarters in the eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops E from BASE to leave BAS, and 'in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is an unfair inclination for or against someone, a synonym for prejudice.

clue.text: Bearing south on excursion leaving runway

parts.note: one's air is one's bearing or manner
S is the compass abbreviation for south
a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: A traveller heads south on an outing and leaves via the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway for aircraft to take off and land.

clue.text: Feeling of resentment beginning to tell in game

parts.note: pique is irritation from wounded pride

indicators.note: beginning takes just the opening letter of tell

explanation.surface: Someone's resentment shows as they start to give away a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes T from tell, which is put after PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is a card game for two players using a 32-card pack.

clue.text: County players in blue

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A county's actors are feeling sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of sad matches downcast, meaning dejected.

clue.text: Gay bar initially visited by Latin, Italian male

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of bar

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A bar is visited by a Latin man from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its old sense of cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe and gay in its older sense both mean carefree and cheerful.
